anomalies.observed: On the Power sheet the MIC26903 (REG2) feedback divider from the output node to FB (NET0164) and from FB to GND is built with R15 = 19k6 (top) and R56 = 1k3 (bottom), with R90 = 6k8 also tied between the output node and FB. Applying the sheet's own formula 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)' gives either 0.8*(1+19.6/1.3) ≈ 12.9 V (if R90 is not in the divider) or 0.8*(1+(19.6k||6.8k)/1.3k) ≈ 3.9 V (if R90 is in parallel with R15). Neither is 5 V.
anomalies.expected: Spec §4.3 states the buck 'steps the battery input down to 5 V' and the block diagram rail is '9A @ 5V max'. The divider must satisfy 0.8*(1+Rtop/Rbot)=5 V, i.e. Rtop/Rbot ≈ 5.25 (e.g. 6.8k over 1.3k). The top feedback resistance as drawn is inconsistent with a 5 V output.

evidence.quote: Power sheet: 'Vout=0.8*(1+R5/R6)' with R15=19k6, R56=1k3, R90=6k8 at FB (NET0164)
§4.3 'A MIC26903YJL-TR synchronous buck regulator steps the battery input down to 5 V ... Block diagram caption: 9A @ 5V max.'

anomalies.impact: The nominal 5 V rail is not regulated to 5 V (it is either grossly over-volted at ~12.9 V, which would exceed the LD39200 6 V absolute-max input and the CH330/servo 5 V loads, or under-volted at ~3.9 V, starving the servo/PWM bank). Either way the board's power tree behaves differently from the intended 5 V design.

parsed.summary: All components, addresses, the 10 mΩ shunt, the 15 µH inductor and the documented known issues (barometer RESET/EOC swap, MAX-8Q label, PCA9685 at 0x41 to avoid a same-bus conflict with the INA219 at 0x40) match the specification; the only deviation I can read off the drawing is the MIC26903 feedback divider, whose resistor values do not yield the specified 5 V output. Confidence is moderate because the divider topology (which resistor is the true top element) is hard to disambiguate on the sheet.
